1.name: Stage 1 — Latent TB Infection (LTBI)
1.summary: Mycobacterium tuberculosis present but contained by the immune system. Patient is asymptomatic and non-contagious.
immediate_care: Confirm with IGRA (QuantiFERON) or TST before starting any therapy
Baseline LFTs, HIV screen, pregnancy test where applicable
Review contacts and index case
Document weight (dosing reference for next steps)

medication.regimen: 3HP preferred — Isoniazid 15 mg/kg + Rifapentine 15 mg/kg weekly × 12 weeks (DOT)
alternatives: 6H or 9H — Isoniazid 5 mg/kg daily × 6-9 months + pyridoxine 25 mg daily
watch_for: Hepatotoxicity — check LFTs at baseline, 1 and 3 months
Peripheral neuropathy — co-prescribe pyridoxine with isoniazid
Rifamycin drug interactions (OCPs, warfarin, HIV ARVs)

nutrition: Vitamin D if deficient; pyridoxine 25 mg/day if on isoniazid

follow_up.visits: Clinic review at weeks 2, 4, then monthly to end of regimen
follow_up.labs: LFTs at baseline, month 1, month 3 (sooner if symptomatic)
follow_up.imaging: No repeat CXR unless symptoms develop
follow_up.endpoint: Document completion; annual symptom screen for 2 years

red_flags: New cough, fever, night sweats, weight loss
patient_education: You are not contagious — no isolation needed
Do not skip doses; set a weekly reminder
Return immediately if yellow eyes/skin or new breathing symptoms
1.warning: Consult doctor if symptoms like cough or fever develop

2.name: Stage 2 — Mild Active Pulmonary TB
2.summary: Early active disease with limited radiographic involvement. Patient is potentially infectious until smear-negative.
immediate_care: Collect 2-3 sputum specimens for AFB smear + Xpert MTB/RIF
Baseline CXR interpretation documented in chart
HIV test, diabetes screen, hepatitis panel, baseline LFTs + renal
Register the case under the national TB program
Start infection-control measures the same day

medication.regimen: HRZE — Isoniazid + Rifampicin + Pyrazinamide + Ethambutol daily for 2 months (intensive phase), then HR daily × 4 months (continuation).
medication.dosing_reference: H 5 mg/kg · R 10 mg/kg · Z 25 mg/kg · E 15 mg/kg (WHO adult bands)
watch_for: Hepatotoxicity — hold all drugs if ALT > 3× ULN with symptoms or 5× ULN asymptomatic
Orange-red body fluids — rifampicin (expected, reassure patient)

2.isolation: Home isolation in a single well-ventilated room until 2 consecutive AFB-negative sputums or clear clinical+bacteriological response (usually 2-3 weeks).
nutrition: Micronutrients: zinc, vitamin A, vitamin D

follow_up.visits: Weekly for first month (DOT), then monthly
follow_up.labs: LFTs at 2 weeks, 1 month, then if symptomatic
follow_up.sputum: Repeat AFB smear at end of month 2 (end of intensive phase) and month 5; convert to culture if smear still positive
follow_up.imaging: CXR at month 2 and end of treatment
follow_up.endpoint: Cured = negative smear at month 5 and end of treatment

patient_education: Cover your mouth; open windows; sleep alone during infectious period
Take every dose — missed doses breed resistance
Expect orange urine, tears, sweat — it is the medicine, not blood
No alcohol until end of continuation phase
2.warning: See doctor immediately if coughing blood

3.name: Stage 3 — Moderate Active TB
3.summary: Extensive pulmonary involvement, often cavitary. High bacillary burden and transmissibility.
immediate_care: Admit if any of: SpO₂ < 92%, severe wasting, hemoptysis, suspected drug resistance
Fit-tested N95 for staff; patient in an airborne-isolation room (AIIR) if hospitalized
Xpert MTB/RIF to rule out rifampicin resistance before starting therapy
Full HIV workup; CD4 if positive, start ART within 2-8 weeks of TB therapy
Nutritional and functional assessment

medication.regimen: HRZE daily × 2 months intensive, then HR daily × 4 months continuation. Consider extending continuation to 7 months if cavitary disease and positive culture at month 2.
adjuncts: Vitamin D + calcium if steroid use
Corticosteroids only for specific indications (e.g., TB meningitis, pericarditis) — not routine
watch_for: Drug-induced hepatitis — low threshold to pause and recheck LFTs
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) in HIV co-infection
Paradoxical worsening — do NOT change regimen without specialist review
medication.resistance_check: If Xpert shows rifampicin resistance, DO NOT start first-line therapy — refer to DR-TB program for MDR workup.

3.isolation: Inpatient AIIR or strict home isolation × minimum 2-3 weeks of effective therapy AND 3 consecutive negative AFB smears. Household contacts screened within 7 days.
nutrition: Supervised supplementation; enteral feeds if oral intake inadequate
Correct anemia, hypoalbuminemia before major interventions

follow_up.visits: DOT daily or 5×/week in intensive phase; weekly in continuation
follow_up.labs: LFTs weekly × 4 weeks, then monthly; CBC monthly; creatinine monthly
follow_up.imaging: CXR at months 2, 5, end of treatment
follow_up.contact_tracing: All close contacts evaluated with symptom screen + CXR + IGRA within 7 days

red_flags: Worsening on therapy after 8 weeks — assess for MDR
patient_education: Stay in your isolation room except for medical visits
Wear a surgical mask whenever you leave the room
DOT means a health worker watches each dose — this is normal and protective
Keep a symptom diary — bring it to every visit
3.warning: Seek emergency care if breathlessness occurs

4.name: Stage 4 — Severe / Advanced TB
4.summary: Extensive bilateral disease, miliary pattern, or complications (respiratory failure, meningitis, disseminated). Potentially life-threatening.
immediate_care: Admit to hospital, airborne isolation room
ABG; oxygen to target SpO₂ ≥ 90%; escalate to NIV/invasive ventilation if indicated
IV access, fluids, correct electrolytes
Empirical HRZE within 24 h after specimens collected — do not wait for culture if clinically unstable
Pulmonology / infectious disease consult same day
Screen and manage complications: cor pulmonale, meningitis, Addisonian crisis (adrenal TB)

medication.regimen: HRZE intensive × 2 months, continuation extended to 7-10 months total (longer in CNS, bone/joint, disseminated). Weight-band dosing adjusted for critical illness and renal/hepatic function.
adjuncts: Corticosteroids (prednisolone 1 mg/kg tapered over 6-8 weeks) for TB meningitis, pericarditis, severe miliary with respiratory failure
ART in HIV: start within 2 weeks of TB therapy if CD4 < 50; else by week 8
watch_for: Hepatic failure — paradoxically higher risk from TB disease itself than drugs; ID input before stopping therapy
Drug accumulation in renal failure (adjust E, Z)
medication.resistance_check: Urgent DST (Xpert MTB/XDR) — assume high resistance risk until proven otherwise.

4.isolation: Strict AIIR for entire inpatient stay AND until documented smear/culture conversion. All visitors in N95. Discharge only when non-infectious AND social support in place.
nutrition: Enteral nutrition day 1 if oral intake impaired; target 1.5-2.0 g protein/kg/day
Refeeding syndrome risk — phosphate/potassium/magnesium monitoring in first week

follow_up.visits: Inpatient daily reviews; post-discharge DOT 5×/week; monthly specialist clinic × 12 months
follow_up.labs: Daily LFTs + U&Es in first week, then per protocol
follow_up.sputum: AFB smear + culture weekly until 2 consecutive negatives, then monthly
follow_up.imaging: CXR weekly until stable, then at months 2, 5, end of treatment; CT if complications
follow_up.rehab: Pulmonary rehabilitation referral post-discharge; mental health screen (TB is a known depression risk)

red_flags: Acute confusion / meningism — lumbar puncture for TB meningitis
Hemodynamic instability — rule out pericardial effusion/tamponade
Severe hyponatremia — SIADH or adrenal TB
Pregnancy — streptomycin contraindicated; coordinate with obstetrics
patient_education: Your family will be screened — this is for their safety, not stigma
Treatment is long (often 9-12 months); every dose counts
Expect fatigue and mood changes — ask for help
Return to ER for: breathlessness at rest, confusion, chest pain, massive hemoptysis
